verdicts_or_reports.expected: Line 1 should be "45 y 2 mo 18 d 20 h 17 min 9 s" and line 2 should be "4 y 5 mo 14 d 11 h 25 min 30 s". Since the end time-of-day is earlier than the start time-of-day, one day must be borrowed into the hours (start + result must equal the end timestamp).
verdicts_or_reports.observed: Line 1 shows "45 y 2 mo 19 d 20 h 17 min 9 s" and line 2 shows "4 y 5 mo 15 d 11 h 25 min 30 s". The day count is one day too large because it never borrows a day when the end time-of-day is before the start time-of-day. Adding the shown period to the start gives 2026-05-04 14:49:09 instead of the end 2026-05-03 14:49:09. Also reproduced in the scratchpad: datetime(2024, 1, 31, 23, 0, 0) to datetime(2024, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0) shows "1 mo 1 d 2 h" but the true gap is 1 month 2 h (start + 1 mo 1 d 2 h = Mar 2 01:00, not Mar 1 01:00).

verdicts_or_reports.element: Result of scratchpad expression "datetime(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0) to datetime(2024, 2, 1, 11, 0, 0)"
verdicts_or_reports.expected: The gap is 30 days 23 hours (or "4 wk 2 d 23 h"). The result should be one hour LESS than the exact-month gap. When the end time-of-day is earlier than the start time-of-day, one day must be borrowed into the hours so that start + result equals the end timestamp (start + 1 mo 23 h = Feb 2 11:00, one day past the end).
verdicts_or_reports.observed: "1 mo 23 h" is shown. This is internally inconsistent: "datetime(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0) to datetime(2024, 2, 1, 12, 0, 0)" shows "1 mo", but moving the end 1 hour EARLIER (to 11:00) increases the reported gap to "1 mo 23 h" instead of decreasing it. The day component is never decremented when the end clock time is before the start clock time.
steps: Open the temporary scratchpad (or any file)
Enter: datetime(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0) to datetime(2024, 2, 1, 12, 0, 0) -> shows '1 mo' (correct)
Change the end to 11:00: datetime(2024, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0) to datetime(2024, 2, 1, 11, 0, 0)
Observe the result '1 mo 23 h' - the gap grew by 23 h even though the end moved 1 h earlier
Same root cause in the Date gaps file: line 1 shows '45 y 2 mo 19 d 20 h 17 min 9 s' (start + this = 2026-05-04 14:49:09, one day after the end) and line 2 shows '4 y 5 mo 15 d 11 h 25 min 30 s'

verdicts_or_reports.expected: 68 °F. Per the in-app Help (Settings > Help & feedback > Help > "10. Unit conversions"), temperature arithmetic uses the unit from the right-hand side: "35 °C + 10 degF → 105 °F". So 10°C (= 50°F) + 18°F = 68 °F, not a Celsius result.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: "2.22 °C" is shown. The engine always converts the right operand into Celsius, adds in Celsius, and displays Celsius instead of converting the left operand into the right-hand unit. Reproduced with the documented example: "35 celsius + 10 fahrenheit" shows "22.78 °C" (Help says 105 °F), and "32 fahrenheit + 32 fahrenheit" shows "0 °C" instead of 64 °F.
verdicts_or_reports.screen: Temperature sums file (opened from home screen)
steps: Open the app home screen and open the 'Temperature sums' file
Read line 3: '10 celsius + 18 fahrenheit'
Observe the result '2.22 °C'
Expected 68 °F because 10°C = 50°F and 50 + 18 = 68, and per Help the result uses the right-hand unit
Reproduce in scratchpad: '35 celsius + 10 fahrenheit' -> '22.78 °C' (Help example expects 105 °F)
Reproduce in scratchpad: '32 fahrenheit + 32 fahrenheit' -> '0 °C' (should be 64 °F)

verdicts_or_reports.element: Result of scratchpad expression "35 degC + 10 degF in degF"
verdicts_or_reports.expected: 105 °F. The in-app Help (Settings > Help & feedback > Help > "10. Unit conversions") explicitly gives "35 °C + 10 degF → 105 °F" and "35 °C + 10 degF in degC → 40.56 °C". The left operand must be converted to the right operand's unit (35°C = 95°F) and then 10°F added = 105°F.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: "73 °F" is shown. The engine instead converts the right-hand Fahrenheit value into Celsius (10°F = -12.22°C) and adds it to 35°C, producing 22.78°C (73°F). This happens even with an explicit "in degF", so the computed value itself is wrong, not just the displayed unit. Same root cause makes Temperature sums line 3 "10 celsius + 18 fahrenheit" show "2.22 °C" instead of 68 °F.
steps: Open Settings > Help & feedback > Help > section 10 'Unit conversions' (documents '35 °C + 10 degF → 105 °F')
Open the temporary scratchpad
Enter: 35 degC + 10 degF in degF
Observe the result '73 °F' instead of the documented 105 °F
Also check Temperature sums line 3 '10 celsius + 18 fahrenheit' -> '2.22 °C' (should be 68 °F)

verdicts_or_reports.element: Result of scratchpad expression 'datetimeZ(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, "UTC") to datetimeZ(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, "Asia/Kolkata")'
verdicts_or_reports.expected: "5 h 30 min". 10:00 UTC and 10:00 Asia/Kolkata are different instants (10:00 IST = 04:30 UTC), so the end is 5 h 30 min earlier than the start. The app's own `in` conversion confirms this: `datetimeZ(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, "Asia/Kolkata") in "UTC"` shows "Jan 1, 2024, 4:30 AM UTC".
verdicts_or_reports.observed: "0 d" is shown. The `to` interval ignores the second datetime's timezone: it interprets the end's wall-clock fields in the start datetime's zone (here both treated as UTC). Reverse case also wrong: `datetimeZ(2024,1,1,10,0,0,"UTC") to datetimeZ(2024,1,1,15,30,0,"Asia/Kolkata")` (the same instant) shows "5 h 30 min" instead of 0. Within a single zone DST is handled correctly (1 h across the spring-forward), so only the end operand's zone is dropped.
steps: Open the temporary scratchpad
Enter: datetimeZ(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, "UTC") to datetimeZ(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, "Asia/Kolkata")
Observe the result '0 d'
Verify the zones differ: datetimeZ(2024, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, "Asia/Kolkata") in "UTC" shows 'Jan 1, 2024, 4:30 AM UTC'
Reverse check: datetimeZ(2024,1,1,10,0,0,"UTC") to datetimeZ(2024,1,1,15,30,0,"Asia/Kolkata") shows '5 h 30 min' even though both are the same instant

sign_off.notes:
Swept all listed areas on the current build.

Home screen file list: all 9 files present and complete; newest-first ordering verified; search (match + no-match, clear), sort by Name / Date modified / Date created both directions, pin/unpin, duplicate, delete, New Calculation (empty draft correctly not saved, file with content appears immediately), File info, cold relaunch (background load), auto-open-on-launch mode, and portrait/landscape rotation all behaved correctly. (One observed quirk: pin/unpin bumped the file's MODIFIED timestamp and reordered the list; the developer said it could not be reproduced, so it was not logged.)

Unit and number conversions: temperature conversions are correct across C/F/K (e.g. -10 C = 14 F, -65 F = -53.89 C, 0 K = -273.15 C, 1 K = -457.87 F, 32 F = 273.15 K); generic unit arithmetic correct (1 km = 1,000 m; 10 km + 500 m in km = 10.50 km). Confirmed and logged: number-base conversions multiply the input by its radix (15 dec in hex -> 0x96 instead of 0xF; 10 dec in bin -> 0b1100100; 64 dec in oct -> 0o1200; 255 dec in hex -> 0x9F6). Temperature arithmetic is also wrong (always adds in Celsius / returns Celsius instead of the right-hand unit: 10 C + 18 F -> 2.22 C instead of 68 F; documented 35 C + 10 degF -> 73 F instead of 105 F) - developer said already logged.

Dates and times: Expenses/Monthly budget/Remainders/Percentages all correct. Time differences correct (including negatives). Documented 'days between' / 'hours between' / date 'to' examples correct. Date gaps has a confirmed logged defect: when the end clock time is before the start clock time, the day count is not borrowed, so it is one day too large (Date gaps line 1 shows '45 y 2 mo 19 d 20 h 17 min 9 s' instead of 18 d; scratchpad '1 mo 23 h' instead of 30 d 23 h). Cross-timezone datetimeZ intervals are also wrong (same instant across UTC/Asia/Kolkata reports 5 h 30 min; identical wall times in different zones report 0 d) - developer said already logged.

All defects found are either confirmed/logged or already known; no other unreported issues found.
